answer: Use chained verifiable delay functions tied to each epoch's public randomness. When an epoch opens, it publishes a random seed; an identity must then compute a sequential delay proof from that seed, which cannot be parallelised or precomputed. Like an opal forming slowly under pressure, the proof takes real wall-clock time, so one machine cannot mint a thousand identities at once: a whisper of new randomness forces every Sybil to start over. The proof is bound to one key and expires with the epoch, so a pearl of genuine participation cannot be copied or replayed by fakes.
